This is not it chief. Goofy ahh story. Main characters feel like side character and we got this happy go lucky solve everything with the power of friendship ahh character. Combat seemed like it was gonna be fun at first, but then I beat a few bosses and like nothing had changed, my characters were doing the same thing and it was boring. Sometimes the enemy show some combinations that are literally impossible to break in your turn so you just get frustrated because you literally have no choice but to get clapped. Is the game pretty, yes, is the music good, of course, but then why is the story so BAD and the gameplay so repetitive, these are the 2 MOST important aspects of RPG and that is literally where this game fails, such a disappointment. Unfortunately I can not recommend this.
While the presentation is stellar that is all the game has to offer.

The story starts out alright (not great) but fails to engage in the long run.
The characters are super flat and forgettable, as is the writing in general. Especially the two protagonists have no personality whatsoever.
Some decisions characters / NPCs made were so devoid of logic or reason that I couldn't take them seriously.

Combat isn't great either. The lock system to prevent enemies from using spells / abilities is annoying.
Normal encounters are tedious and too drawn out. After only a few hours I tried my best to avoid any encounter I possibly could which I usually never do in a (J)RPG.

The wheels minigame was pretty fun though, probably the best thing about this game besides the graphics.

The combat system/abilities never really expanded from the start of the game. I was expecting either more characters, or more abilities. At its core, combat is the meat and potatoes of a RPG.

It was fun to explore the maps, and the game was courteous of your time, always sure to have shortcuts to make backtracking as painless as possible.

While I most likely will beat the game for the base ending, I don't think it is a great enough game to recommend to someone. Sideways thumb.

I have mixed feelings about this game.

It isn't "bad" at all. The pixel art and animation is great! The music is exceptional! There is a minigame that comes up often that I found pretty enjoyable, and it breaks up the normal game play nicely. Some of the humor is a little bit simple, but sometimes I chuckled. The "dungeon designs" were neat! But again, a little bit simple for my taste.

The thing is, I was told this was going to be like a modernized Chrono Trigger... In some ways, the battles do incorporate some aspects of that legendary SNES game, but to juxtapose the two at all is... Frankly, they are not in the same realm.

The story of this game and puzzles seem to be targeted towards young teens. There is nothing wrong with that! I just wasn't the target audience, perhaps.

Overall, this is a pretty decent game! It just seems a little basic for my standards. The plot is predictable and I was never really "excited" to advance. BUT, I am sure this is a great entry gate for young people to try an RPG that has a battle system and a story that isn't overly complicated.

6.5 / 10

I disagree with the negative reviews. I think the issue is that a lot of people had too high expectations.

From what I learned, having high expectations that is ALWAYS going to make the game a disappointment. That’s what made me so disappointed in Chrono Trigger ironically enough.

I will admit I have not finished the story as of now but I will say this: I love the combat and the characters. The combat is no joke and you can easily lose if you do not strategize well enough. That, to me, is what makes winning these battles so rewarding. There have been many times I just NARROWLY escaped losing a battle. It’s exhilarating, and easily what I love the most about this game.

Admittedly, I’m one of those people that cares more about the gameplay than the story. But so far? I like it. It’s nothing crazy, nothing like say, Xenoblade Chronicles (my favorite rpg of all time), but there are definitely some moments that keep me interested in how things are going to end up.

Overall, I’m having fun. And that’s all that matters to me.

What can I say that hasn't already been said about this game? The music is fantastic, the style and pixel graphics are legit amazing, the characters are all unique and got so much personality to them, and the gameplay is fun and deep enough to be engaging but not too difficult. Everything I know the developers sent out to do. This game is truly a callback and inspired by old rpgs but a modern look and feel to it. Its story has enough wonder and mystery to it that you can imagine and fill in the blanks like older rpgs but does enough to suck you in. I've seen some complaints that it isn't deep enough or explain enough like other rpgs or other games in general. That isn't what it is trying to do. This game and the developers just want you to dive into this world and experience everything it is offering. All the laughs, wonder, darkness, and fun it has to offer. It is truly worth your time and money and you will not regret buying it and trying it out. I will truly remember this game as one of my favorites, not because it is "the best game i've ever played" but because it did everything just right and made it a truly memorable experience.
This game is so fun and I enjoy it. Reminds me of the old final fantasy games.

As a classic RPG fan I give this game an 8.5/10. The art is great, music is good and the characters are fun. This game would be a 10/10 if it were slightly more complex at times and the pacing of the story was better fleshed out. Just because I didn't give it a 10/10 doesn't mean that I don't think this game is GREAT. This is a Great game for any rpg fan. I also think it's a great game for NEW RPG players. I think that is what some of the reviewers are missing. There are tons of new people discovering rpgs for the first time. They don't all need to be mega difficult or complex. If you are looking for a beautiful, fun and chill RPG to play, then pick up Sea of Stars.

Sea of Stars is honestly one of my favourite games I have ever played. Every section of the game feels expertly crafted and designed to be fun to play through. You are missing out on one of the best RPGs of all time if you don't play this one. Do. not. sleep. on. this. game.

After 26 hours into the Game, here's what I think. Loved the game's story, soundtrack (amazing) animations and characters. The puzzle where good. The combat was ok, but honestly it needs more variety of base skills to make it less repetitive. The only think that I really didn't like was the last part, it feels rushed and the ending feels unsatisfying, at least for me. The characters background is ignored and there's this really sad feeling that the great plot twists, background story and lore for all the characters (even the enemies) is wasted. You dont even get to fight the "real" final boss per se. I don't want to spoil anything so Im trying to give the least amount of information, but darn, that ending really ruined the Game for me. It could have been so much better and could have been such a longer Game, it makes me really sad for the potential and lore wasted into the endgame. TL;DR: A fun and emotional gameplay, ruined by a lazy ending of what could have been a perfect RPG.

First off, Sea of Stars does a lot of things right!

The art style is very pleasing to look at. The combat, animations and controls are indeed very good. This game is very enjoyable to play, mostly.

However, the story telling just doesn't deliver. This is pretty unfortunate for such a beautiful game, but I consider a compelling story to be the natural core of an RPG. Here, the story is outright boring. The characters don't seem to have any character of themselves and make unbelievable choices that make it hard for you to relate or connect to them. The dialogue is uninteresting and rich in filler.

I also need to quickly mention the music which sounds a bit sloppy and can get annoying at times.

Unfortunately, I can't recommend it.

If you enjoyed the story of The Messenger, you will enjoy Sea of Stars.

I thought it did a great job at tying both games' stories together. Every thought I had about a potential plot conflict was addressed at some point in the game. The Messenger is foreshadowed and referenced many times with varying degrees of subtlety, enough that I wanted to replay it again after completing Sea of Stars to see what I had missed. SoS even perpetuates the blatant disregard for time travel logic that Messenger leans into so heavily. ;)

If you do only plan on playing through each game once, I recommend playing them in order of release. While many of the references between the games are "bidirectional", most of the subtler ones are found in SoS.

This is my first review. Playing through this game I was able to see the developers put in A LOT of effort into this game. Graphics are pristine, storyline is well written, game is fun and I haven't run into any glitches. I highly recommend if you're looking for a fully immersive experience to binge-play. I thought the end game developer easter egg was a nice touch. 10/10 for me, can't wait to see what Sabotage brings next
